<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Let me try clicking on the yellow dot (node 10) at rows 20-21, cols 24-25
# to see if it switches the active cursor
result = action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 20, 'col': 24}])
print(f"Click yellow: board_changed={last_action_result.get('board_changed')}, gameplay_changed={last_action_result.get('gameplay_changed')}")

# Check what changed
before = last_transition.before_frame.segmentation
after = last_transition.after_frame.segmentation

before_nodes = {n['id']: n for n in before['nodes']}
after_nodes = {n['id']: n for n in after['nodes']}

changes = []
all_ids = set(list(before_nodes.keys()) + list(after_nodes.keys()))
for nid in sorted(all_ids):
    bn = before_nodes.get(nid)
    an = after_nodes.get(nid)
    if bn is None:
        changes.append(f"Node {nid} appeared: color={an['color']}, px={an['pixels']}")
    elif an is None:
        changes.append(f"Node {nid} disappeared")
    else:
        for key in ['color', 'pixels', 'hash', 'boundary', 'children']:
            if bn[key] != an[key]:
                changes.append(f"Node {nid} {key}: {bn[key]} -> {an[key]}")

print("Changes:")
for c in changes:
    print(f"  {c}")

# Check both cursor positions
seg = current_frame.segmentation
for n in seg['nodes']:
    if n['color'] in ('N', 'Y'):
        b = n['boundary']
        min_r = min(p[0] for p in b)
        min_c = min(p[1] for p in b)
        print(f"  {n['color']} dot: top-left=({min_r},{min_c}), px={n['pixels']}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
